claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic FCC CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy with a homogeneous coarse-grained microstructure.
Room-temperature ECAP will produce ultrafine grain refinement in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Annealing at approximately 600°C for 30 minutes will relax high-energy grain boundaries without significant grain growth.
Adjusting annealing time or temperature using in situ or quasi-in situ EBSD will optimize the formation of low-energy, coherent grain boundaries.
ECAP followed by controlled sub-recrystallization annealing will create a nanostructured microstructure with a high fraction of low-energy special grain boundaries.
ECAP-induced grain refinement increases yield strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Controlled annealing changes the grain-boundary character in favor of low-energy coherent interfaces.
Low-energy coherent boundaries facilitate efficient dislocation transmission and boundary-mediated plasticity.
Improved dislocation transmission and boundary-mediated plasticity preserve or enhance tensile ductility.
Optimized grain boundaries reduce crack-initiation sites and thereby improve fracture toughness.
Reducing microstructural defects produces a modest increase in Young’s modulus.
The processed alloy will exhibit a 20–30% increase in yield strength relative to conventionally processed coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi.
The processed alloy will maintain or slightly enhance ductility relative to conventionally processed coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi.
The processed alloy will improve fracture toughness relative to conventionally processed coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi.
The processed alloy will have a modestly higher Young’s modulus than conventionally processed coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi.
Excessive grain growth or a non-optimal grain-boundary configuration will prevent the predicted property enhancements.
The strategy will be ineffective if ECAP does not produce sufficient grain refinement.
Intrinsic alloy characteristics may impede the development of low-energy grain boundaries.
